overview: Fort Peabody is a rare surviving Colorado National Guard redoubt associated with the state’s hard-rock labor conflict of 1903–1904.
History Colorado records that a local Guard unit constructed the position in early 1904 at more than 13,000 feet near the Ouray–San Miguel county line.

timeline.text: Fort Peabody is a rare surviving Colorado National Guard redoubt associated with the state’s hard-rock labor conflict of 1903–1904.
Fort Peabody is a rare surviving Colorado National Guard redoubt associated with the state’s hard-rock labor conflict of 1903–1904.
The site was listed in the National Register of Historic Places in 2005 for its military, industrial, and social-history significance, with 1904 identified as its significant year.

A San Miguel County preservation account records a Colt rapid-fire gun at the post and later restoration/preservation work on the surviving guardhouse in 2010 under county/GMUG National Forest direction.

moreHistory: The defensive site consisted of a small wooden guardhouse, a flag mount, and a stone emplacement described in period and preservation sources as a sniper or rapid-fire-gun position.
Troops occupied the fortification until martial law was revoked in June 1904.
The site was listed in the National Register of Historic Places in 2005 for its military, industrial, and social-history significance, with 1904 identified as its significant year.
San Miguel County preservation records document later stabilization and continuing maintenance of the surviving resource.

Component safeguard: treat the guardhouse, flag-mount location, stone defensive emplacement, and surrounding National Register site as parts of one Fort Peabody complex rather than separate discovery locations.
